LESSON: LANGUAGE USE 15.3.1 IMPERATIVES (COMMANDS) INTERJECTIONS OF EXCITEMENT/JOY

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade two
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES
Strand: Strand 15
Topic 15.3: Language Use 15.3.1 Imperatives (commands) Interjections of excitement/joy
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Language Use 15.3.1 Imperatives (commands) Interjections of excitement/joy, part of Strand 15 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade two ENGLISH LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES.

Key inquiry question: What commands do we give to each other? 2.When do we use interjections of excitement or joy?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Language Use 15.3.1 Imperatives (commands) Interjections of excitement/joy together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication and Collaboration as learner participates with peers through pair/ group work.

● Creativity and imagination as learner engages in dialogues/ role play with peers.

Values:
Responsibility as learner responds to commands and interjection appropriately.

Link to

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Life Skills : Effective communication is enhanced as learner gains knowledge on appropriate use of commands and interjections

Link to other Learning Areas:

Interjections and imperatives are learnt in Kiswahili and Kenyan Sign Language Activities.
